rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣāʿiqa is what strikes them, namely death, as the next verse says they were raised after dying.
rows.anchor: يعني ما تصعقون منه، أي: تموتون، لأنه قال:

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses al-ṣāʿiqa as death.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الصاعقة: الموت (¬2)، ومضى الكلام في الصاعقة

words: لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهْرَةً
rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes say God sent Moses with seventy Israelite notables to repent from calf worship; after hearing God, they demanded direct sight when the cloud lifted, and a heavenly fire consumed them.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن الله تعالى أمر موسى أن يأتيه في ناس من بني إسرائيل يعتذرون إليه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says they watched one another as the thunderbolt descended.
rows.anchor: يريد نظر بعضهم إلى بعض عند نزول الصاعقة (¬5)، قاله (¬6) ابن زيد

words: لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهْرَةً
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were punished for refusing faith in Moses after his miracle until they could see God; believing a messenger after a manifest miracle is obligatory, and demanding further signs is impermissible.
rows.anchor: لأنهم امتنعوا من الإيمان بموسى بعد ظهور معجزته حتى يريهم ربهم جهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked from faith, confirmation, and longing, whereas these people asked doubtingly, denying, and obstinately, so only they were punished.
rows.anchor: ولما كان سؤال موسى إيمانا منه وتصديقا واشتياقا لم يعاقب عليه

words: لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهْرَةً
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Moses’ companions believed seeing God impossible and used it to mean they would never believe, like the impossible condition in 7:40; hence their punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إن أصحاب موسى اعتقدوا إحالة الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes them for opposing a messenger despite his miracle, as their forebears opposed Moses, and warns the present audience against the same fate.
rows.anchor: تتضمن التوبيخ لهم على مخالفة الرسول عليه السلام مع قيام معجزته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exchanged the small gain of worldly life for the great gain of the hereafter.
rows.anchor: أي: استبدلوا قليل الدنيا بكثير الاخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is not reduced; khiffa literally denotes a decrease in weight.
rows.anchor: أي: لا ينقص، والخفة: نقصان الوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ links this clause to their act of buying, making it part of the relative description of those people.
rows.anchor: ودخلت الفاء في قوله: {فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب} للعطف على (اشتروا)

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines naskh linguistically as canceling one thing and putting another in its place, as the sun removes the shade and takes its place.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: النسخ في اللغة: إبطال شيء وإقامة آخر مقامه

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another authority explains succession as the passing of one age or generation and the arrival of another to take its place.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: تناسخ الأزمنة والقرن بعد القرن: هو مضي الأول ومجيء الثاني بعده يخلفه في محله

rows.speaker: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī distinguishes replacing one thing with another from transferring a thing to a new place while it remains the same.
rows.anchor: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي: النسخ: تبديل الشيء من الشيء، وهو غيره، والنسخ: نقل شيء من مكان إلى مكان

rows.speaker: الفراء وأبو سعيد
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and Abū Saʿīd use masakha and nasakha for turning someone into an ape as equivalent expressions.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو تراب (¬4) عن الفراء وأبي سعيد: مسخه الله قردا، ونسخه قردا، بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: العلماء من أهل اللغة والتفسير
rows.claim: Linguists and exegetes give naskh two senses, the first being to copy a book into another copy.
rows.anchor: وقال العلماء من أهل اللغة والتفسير (¬1): النسخ له معنيان:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the copying sense, istinsākh in 45:29 may mean making a copy, like istaskhara meaning sakhira, or summoning the angels to write; both mean writing without copying from a physical exemplar.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا قوله عز وجل {إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون} [الجاثية: 29]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the copying sense, the entire Qurʾan is a transcription from the Mother of the Book to the Prophet before being sent down to him.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا المعنى: القرآن كله منسوخ،

rows.speaker: العلماء من أهل اللغة والتفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is lifting and nullifying a ruling, either with a replacement or without one; the verse intends this sense.
rows.anchor: والثاني: هو رفع الحكم وإبطاله، ثم يجوز النسخ إلى بدل وإلى غير بدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation in the Qurʾan includes a ruling that is lifted while its wording remains written and recited but is no longer acted upon; this is the familiar form.
rows.anchor: منها: ما يكون حكمه مرفوعا، وخطه مثبت يتلى ويقرأ

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has power over everything, including abrogation, substitution, and all else.
rows.anchor: أي: من النسخ والتبديل وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is an admonitory affirmation: it expects agreement, as in the poetic question, You are the best riders of camels.
rows.anchor: هو استفهام معناه التوقيف والتقرير (¬7)،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kingdom of the heavens and earth means complete and perfected power: God owns them and all within them, and knows what benefits people in the laws imposed through abrogation.
rows.anchor: الملك: تمام القدرة واستحكامها (¬2)، وقد مر. ومعنى الآية: أنه يملك السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walī is on the faʿīl pattern with the active sense of fāʿil, meaning an administrator or one who takes charge.
rows.anchor: هو فعيل بمعنى الفاعل (¬4)، يقال: هو والي الأمر ووليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that people have no protector or helper besides God recalls the discussion of walī at 2:257 and warns that none can ward off His punishment.
rows.anchor: معنى الولي عند قوله: {الله ولي الذين آمنوا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says fīhim means among my descendants; the pronoun can refer either to Abraham’s descendants or to the community called a Muslim nation, both identified here as Arabs descended from Abraham.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: في ولدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the requested messenger from among them as Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Abraham’s prayer by sending Muhammad from among his people as the master of the prophets.
rows.anchor: فاستجاب الله دعاءه، وبعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم، محمدا سيد الأنبياء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says his status as the Seal of Prophets was written in the Mother of the Book while Adam was still being formed; this was Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’ good news in 61:6, and his mother’s vision of a light illuminating Syrian palaces.
rows.anchor: لذلك قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Book is the revealed Qurʾan and what it contains of duties, rulings, Prophetic practices, and the laws of earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد القرآن الذي أنزل عليه، وما فيه من الفرائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn ʿAbbās’s reading, wisdom is the Book itself, paired with it because the two terms differ in wording.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا الحكمة: هي نفس الكتاب، وجمع بينهما لاختلاف اللفظين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses wisdom as understanding the Qurʾan, in line with the lexical sense of comprehending meanings.
rows.anchor: والحكمة في اللغة: فهم المعاني، وبه قال مجاهد، فإنه قال:

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim defines wisdom as knowledge joined to action; a person is not called wise unless both are present.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسلم: هي العلم والعمل، ولا يسمى الرجل حكيما

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd calls any saying that admonishes, rebukes, urges virtue, or restrains wrongdoing wisdom.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن دريد يقول: كل كلمة وعظتك أو زجرتك أو دعتك إلى مكرمة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying states that some poetry contains wisdom.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -:

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī traces the word to restraint: a judge restrains a person from injustice, and a bridle restrains an animal.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي: أصل الحكومة: رد الرجل عن الظلم، ومنه سميت حكمة اللجام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiya linguistically attributes growth in untainted good deeds; zakāt means increase.
rows.anchor: أصل التزكية في اللغة: النسبة إلى الازدياد من الأفعال الحسنة التي ليست بمشوبة، والزكاة: الزيادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as guiding them to the best of worship.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ويرشدهم إلى أفضل عبادتك

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it means purifying them from associationism and freeing them from it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج (¬2): يطهرهم من الشرك، ويخلصهم منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the messenger collects the alms due on their wealth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يأخذ زكاة أموالهم (¬4)، وقال ابن كيسان:

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysān says the messenger will testify for them as just on Judgment Day because they testify that the prophets conveyed their messages.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: يشهد لهم يوم القيامة بالعدالة إذا شهدوا للأنبياء بالبلاغ

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق والمفضل
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq and al-Mufaḍḍal gloss al-ʿAzīz as the One who is inaccessible and cannot be overcome; this derives from strength, though God is not described by physical severity.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو إسحاق: العزيز في صفات الله: الممتنع فلا يغلبه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author allows divine ʿizza as invulnerability and transcendence beyond reach, but rejects describing God simply as severe or physically strong.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز في وصف الله تعالى الشدة (¬7)، ويجوز العزة، وهي امتناعه على من أراده

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الشيباني
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī’s verse uses taʿazzaza for flesh becoming firm and strong as a camel grows lean, evidencing the root sense of strength.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو عمرو الشيباني (¬1): أجد إذا ضمرت تعزز لحمها

rows.speaker: أبو كبير الهذلي
rows.claim: Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī calls a powerful bird of prey ʿazīza; the author also cites azāz for hard ground as evidence of the root’s sense of severity.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو كبير الهذلي (¬3) يصف عقابا (¬4): حتى انتهيت إلى فراش عزيزة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-ʿAzīz is the One whose like cannot be found.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: العزيز: الذي لا يوجد مثله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ derives al-ʿAzīz from ʿazza yaʿizzu, to be so rare that it is scarcely found.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال: عز يعز بالكسر: إذا قل حتى لا يكاد يوجد، عزة فهو عزيز

rows.speaker: الكسائي وابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, Ibn al-Anbārī, and other linguists define al-ʿAzīz as powerful and dominant, citing the Arabic verb for overcoming and 38:23.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي (¬6) وابن الأنباري (¬7) وجماعة من أهل اللغة: العزيز: القوي الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the command about retaliation, kutiba means prescribed and made obligatory, as it does in the bequest verse.
rows.anchor: كتب هاهنا، بمعنى: فرض وأوجب، كقوله: {كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb comes from writing something down to secure it from being forgotten, so it came to mean firmly imposing an obligation.
rows.anchor: وأصله: أن من أراد إحكام شيء والاستيثاق منه كتبه؛ لئلا ينساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation connects kutiba with God’s decree in the Preserved Tablet, meaning He decreed and settled the matter, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أصله: ما كتبه الله في اللوح المحفوظ، ومن هذا قوله: {كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb can also mean made or appointed, as in the cited verses about faith, witnesses, and what God will grant.
rows.anchor: ويكون (كتب) بمعنى (¬1): جعل، كقوله: {أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that someone is certain death is near, sees its signs, and has no doubt it is approaching.
rows.anchor: يعني: إذا تيقن حضور الموت، ورأى أعلامه، ولم يشكك في قربه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death’s arrival refers to its causes and preliminaries, such as illness; bequest was obligatory earlier but becomes urgent when those signs arise and may not be delayed.
rows.anchor: يريد: أسباب الموت ومقدماته، من العلل والأمراض. وكان الإيصاء فرضا قبل نزول أسباب الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing does not mean the duty began only at death’s onset: al-waṣiyya can mean the act of bequeathing, or the long separation between verb and noun can compensate for the feminine ending.
rows.anchor: لأنه أراد بالوصية الإيصاء، أو للفصل بين الفعل والوصية؛ لأن الكلام لما طال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-waṣiyya is nominative either as a passive construction or as the subject, with li-l-wālidayn as its predicate; either whole clause is governed by kutiba.
rows.anchor: ورفع {الوصية} من وجهين: أحدهما: على ما لم يسم فاعله، والثاني: على الابتداء، ويكون {للوالدين} الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr is a general term for property and other good things, but often denotes money in the Qurʾan, as in 2:272, 100:8, and 28:24.
rows.anchor: الخير: اسم جامع للمال وغيره، والخير يراد به المال في كثير من القرآن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bequest should be in a fair amount that discerning people recognize as free of injustice; it must not exceed one third.
rows.anchor: أي: بالشيء الذي يعلم ذوو التمييز أنه لا حيف فيه، فهو العدل الذي لا ينكر، يعني: لا يزيد على الثلث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaqqan affirms that this is genuinely incumbent on you.
rows.anchor: أي: حق ذلك عليكم حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people described as God-fearing are believers who avoid associationism.
rows.anchor: أي: المؤمنين الذين يتقون الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that the verse’s ruling was abrogated, though they later differ over whether the abrogation covered all bequests or only those to heirs.
rows.anchor: وقد اجتمعت العلماء على نسخ هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion was that pre-Islamic Arabs ostentatiously bequeathed wealth to distant people while leaving dependents destitute; the verse redirected bequests to family and kin until inheritance verses replaced that rule.
rows.anchor: وكان السبب في نزول هذه الآية: أن أهل الجاهلية كانوا يوصون بمالهم للبعداء رياء وسمعة، ويتركون العيال عالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance rules abrogated the mandatory bequest to parents and other relatives who inherit, in light of the Prophetic rule that no heir receives a bequest.
rows.anchor: فأجمعوا على نسخ الوصية للوالدين والأقربين الذين يرثون

rows.speaker: مسلم بن يسار والعلاء بن زياد ومسروق والحسن
rows.claim: These authorities hold that the bequest duty remains for kin who do not inherit, including parents excluded by unbelief or enslavement; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says dying without such a bequest ends one’s work in sin.
rows.anchor: وهو (¬2) مذهب مسلم بن يسار، والعلاء بن زياد (¬3) (¬4)، ومسروق (¬5) والحسن (¬6)، حتى قال # الضحاك: من مات ولم يوص لذي قرابته

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Ṭāwūs says that when someone bequeaths to outsiders while leaving kin, the gift should be taken from the outsiders and returned to the relatives.
rows.anchor: وقال طاوس: إن أوصى للأجانب (¬2) وترك ذوي قرابته نزع منهم، ورد إلى ذوي قرابته

rows.speaker: الأكثرون من العلماء
rows.claim: The majority, whose position the author says is practiced today, hold that the whole ruling is abrogated: no bequest is required for any relative or stranger, though one may be made for anyone except an heir.
rows.anchor: والأكثرون من العلماء -وهو الذي يعمل به اليوم- على أن حكم الآية كله (¬5) منسوخ، ولا تجب على أحد وصية لأحد قريب ولا بعيد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd reports consensus among scholars of the Ḥijāz, Tihāma, Iraq, and Syria, including Sufyān, Mālik, al-Awzāʿī, and al-Layth: bequests are permitted for all except heirs but are not obligatory.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: وعلى هذا القول أجمعت العلماء من أهل الحجاز وتهامة والعراق والشام، منهم سفيان ومالك الأوزاعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here khayr means substantial wealth.
rows.anchor: والخير في هذه الآية حمل على المال الكثير

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: When an ill man wanted to bequeath, ʿAlī cited the verse and advised him to leave his small amount to his dependents because that was better.
rows.anchor: فقد روي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه دخل على مريض يعوده، فقال: إني أريد أن أوصي

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha told a man with three thousand and four dependents that this was only a small amount and he should leave it to his family.
rows.anchor: وروي أيضا أن رجلا قال لعائشة رضي الله عنها: إني أريد أن أوصي، قالت: كم مالك؟ قال: ثلاثة آلاف

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd explains the distributive wording of his example: the ruler gave each person a garment and one hundred.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: أتينا الأمير فكسانا كلنا حلة وأعطى كلنا مائة، قال:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, ʿAlqama, Ibn Shihāb, and most scholars say fasting initially allowed a choice to fast or feed one poor person instead; 2:185 abrogated that option.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كانت الإطاقة أن الرجل أو المرأة كان يصبح صائما، ثم إن شاء أفطر وأطعم لذلك مسكينا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says voluntary goodness means adding charity beyond the one mudd that had been due from someone able to fast who broke the fast before abrogation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: زاد في الصدقة، يعنى: على المد الواحد

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Suddī say the volunteer feeds two poor people, increasing the charity beyond the required amount.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد (¬4) والسدى (¬5): يطعم مسكينين

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب
rows.claim: Ibn Shihāb interprets it as voluntarily fasting on the day for which the fidya would have been paid.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن شهاب: يريد: من صام الفدية فهو خير له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name shahr derives from visibility or public recognition: the month is prominent in dealings, debts, and ritual observances people need to schedule.
rows.anchor: الشهر: مأخوذ من الشهرة، تقول شهر الشيء يشهره شهرا: إذا أظهره

rows.speaker: الليث وابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Al-Layth and Ibn al-Aʿrābī explain the moon’s name as month by its visibility: it becomes apparent or is made conspicuous.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: والشهر: ظهور الشيء، وسمي (¬2) الهلال شهرا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the crescent is called a month because it is visible and clear.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: سمي الهلال شهرا لشهرته وبيانه

rows.speaker: بعضهم؛ ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Some say the month is named for the crescent: Arabs say they saw the month to mean its new moon, as witnessed by Dhū al-Rumma’s line using al-shahr for the crescent.
rows.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: يرى الشهر قبل الناس وهو بخيل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says he has heard no verb from the word except ashhernā, meaning a month has arrived for us.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: ولم أسمع منه فعلا إلا هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes shahr an appositive for al-ṣiyām, yielding the sense that fasting Ramadan was prescribed.
rows.anchor: وارتفع على البدل من الصيام، كأن المعنى: كتب عليكم شهر رمضان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes shahr the subject of an independent clause, with the relative clause as its predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ابتداء، وخبره الذي مع صلته، كقولك: زيد الذي في الدار

rows.speaker: الأخفش والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ parse the phrase as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning this is Ramadan, which explains the previously mentioned numbered days.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: ارتفع على أنه خبر ابتداء محذوف، المعنى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds it more fitting to make alladhī an adjective for the month, explicitly requiring its fast; if it were the predicate, the text would only report that the Qurʾan was revealed in it.
rows.anchor: قال: والأشبه أن يكون {الذي} وصفا، ليكون النص قد وقع على الأمر بصيام الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred parsing, naming the month again in whoever is present during it honors and emphasizes it, as in the repeated openings of 69:1–2 and 101:1–2.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله: {الحاقة (1) ما الحاقة} [الحاقة:1 - 2] و {القارعة (1) ما القارعة} [القارعة:1 - 2]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ before man shahida is unexpected for the predicate of an independent subject; the author postpones its discussion until that phrase is reached.
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله: {فمن شهد} داخل على خبر الابتداء، وليس من حق خبر الابتداء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the whole Qurʾan descended from the Preserved Tablet on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel delivered it to Muhammad in installments over twenty years.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ في ليلة القدر من شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, an interpretation chosen by al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl, says the Qurʾan was revealed concerning Ramadan’s merit.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: {أنزل فيه القرآن} معناه: أنزل في فضله القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says it was revealed regarding the obligation to fast Ramadan, just as revelation concerning alms or wine can refer to their legal rulings.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنبارى: أنزل في فرضه وإيجاب صومه على الخلق القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾan names God’s speech, and authorities disagree over whether the name is derived and whether it takes a hamza.
rows.anchor: فأما (¬5) القرآن فهو اسم لكلام الله تعالى # واختلفوا (¬1) في اشتقاقه وهمزه،

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the word without a hamza.
rows.anchor: فقرأه ابن كثير بغير همز

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī treats Qurʾan as an unhamzated name for God’s Book, not derived from qaraʾa; the author says this suggests a proper name like Torah or Gospel.
rows.anchor: أن الشافعي، رحمه الله، كان يقول: القرآن اسم، وليس بمهموز، ولم يؤخذ من قرأت،

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: Another group likewise treats Qurʾan as an un-derived proper name for God’s speech, analogous to those who regard the name Allah as non-derived.
rows.anchor: وقد قال بهذا جماعة، قالوا: إنه اسم كلامه، يجرى مجرى الأعلام في أسماء غيره،

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others derive the name from qarana, to join things: its chapters, verses, and letters are joined together, so the form qirān is unhamzated.
rows.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أنه مأخوذ من قرنت الشيء بالشيء: إذا ضممت أحدهما إلى الآخر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan means guiding, a circumstantial expression that supplies the second object of anzala.
rows.anchor: أي: هاديا، وهو حال قد سد مسد المفعول الثاني لأنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyināt is coordinated with hudan, so the verse says the Qurʾan was sent as clarification for people.
rows.anchor: و {بينات} عطف على قوله {هدى}،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyināt is the plural of bayyina and means clear, evident proofs.
rows.anchor: والبينات: جمع بينة، يقال: بان الشيء يبين بيانا فهو بين، مثل: بيع بمعنى بايع. والبينات: الواضحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance includes what is lawful and forbidden, legal limits, and rulings.
rows.anchor: يريد: من الحلال والحرام والحدود والأحكام

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that guidance is direction toward God’s pleasure and the Furqān distinguishes truth from falsehood and clarifies what to do or leave; al-Wāḥidī refers to his earlier explanation at 2:53.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وبينات من الهدى}: يريد: من الرشاد إلى مرضاة الله، {والفرقان} يريد: فرق فيه بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمازني
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Māzinī call the fāʾ redundant because here it marks neither coordination nor a conditional consequence; they cite 62:8 and a poetic line with two fāʾs, one unnecessary after idhā.
rows.anchor: زعم الأخفش والمازني: أن الفاء ههنا زائدة، وذلك أن الفاء تدخل للعطف أو للجزاء أو زيادة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī argues the fāʾ can mark a conditional result: Ramadan is a generic, not uniquely specified month, and the command means whoever witnesses the month in which the Qurʾan was revealed must fast it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: ولا يمتنع (¬1) أن يكون دخول الفاء لمعنى الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahida means to be present; its object is omitted, with the sense of being present at one’s town or home rather than traveling.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {شهد} أي: حضر. ومعنى الشهود في اللغة: الحضور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-shahr is an adverb of time, not a direct object, since everyone experiences the month; the intended meaning is being at home during it.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {الشهر} انتصابه على الظرف، ولا يجوز أن يكون مفعولا به؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse assumes the witness is rational, adult, resident, and healthy for fasting to be obligatory.
rows.anchor: ولا بد أيضا من إضمار حال الشاهد وصفته، التي بوجودها يجب الصوم، وهو أن يقال: من شهد منكم الشهر عاقلا بالغا مقيما صحيحا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر أهل التأويل
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most exegetes read it as fasting the part of the month one witnesses; a person who travels during the month may break the fast.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأكثر أهل التأويل: معناه: فليصم ما شهد منه؛ لأنه إن سافر في حال الشهر كان له الإفطار

rows.speaker: النخعي والسدي وابن سيرين
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī, al-Suddī, Ibn Sīrīn, and a group hold that someone resident at the beginning of the month may not break the fast after traveling.
rows.anchor: قول النخعي (¬4) والسدي (¬5) وابن سيرين (¬6)

words: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sick and traveler exemption is repeated because the earlier command to fast could otherwise suggest the abrogation removed everyone’s former option; its repetition confirms their dispensation remains.
rows.anchor: أعاد هاهنا تخيير المريض والمسافر وترخيصهما في الإفطار؛ لأن الله تعالى ذكر في الآية الأولى تخيير المقيمين بقوله: {فليصمه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may break the fast for any illness likely to worsen beyond what they can bear; if fasting exhausts the person, they should break it.
rows.anchor: هو كل مرض كان الأغلب من أمر صاحبه بالصوم الزيادة في علته زيادة لا يحتمله، والأصل فيه: أنه إذا أجهده الصوم أفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey that permits breaking the fast is sixteen farsakhs or more.
rows.anchor: وحد السفر الذي يبيح الإفطار (¬1): ستة عشر فرسخا (¬2) فصاعدا

rows.speaker: عامة الفقهاء
rows.claim: Most jurists regard breaking the fast as a divine concession for travelers: one who breaks it accepts the concession, and one who fasts fulfills the obligation.
rows.anchor: والإفطار رخصة من الله للمسافر، فمن (¬3) أفطر فبرخصة الله أخذ، ومن صام ففرضه أدى، على هذا عامة الفقهاء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s statement that fasting while traveling is not righteousness is directed at a traveler whom fasting strains and exhausts; fasting is disliked for that person.
rows.anchor: ومن أجهده الصوم في السفر كره له ذلك

rows.speaker: قوم من الصحابة
rows.claim: Some Companions hold that breaking the fast during travel is obligatory.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم من الصحابة إلى أن الإفطار في السفر واجب
